name: get_engine_info
description: Returns the engine's version, platform, launch settings and package status. Call it first, to check that the engine is new enough and to see which toolchain packages are installed. It is fast and local: it never uses the network. Missing packages are installed automatically by the tools that need them, unless auto_install is off.

version.description: The package release, as a date tag (yyyy-mm-dd).

PackageStatus.description: Whether a package is ready to use.

oneOf.description: Installed and intact.
Not installed.

Installed but incomplete or damaged. It is repaired when a tool needs
it, unless auto-install is off.

outputSchema.description: The engine's version, platform, launch settings and package status.

auto_install.description:
Whether the engine installs and repairs packages automatically when a
tool needs them. On by default. The host turns it off with the
--no-auto-install command-line argument.

command_line.description: The command-line arguments the engine was launched with, as given.

engine_folder.description:
The engine folder, as the host set it with the --engine-folder
command-line argument. The engine keeps its packages and logs there.

engine_version.description:
The engine release, as a date tag (yyyy-mm-dd, or yyyy-mm-dd-N for a
later release on the same day). Compare versions by date.

The log file this engine process writes, in the logs subfolder of the
engine folder. Useful when reporting a problem.

name: install_packages
description: Installs or repairs the engine's toolchain packages, downloading them from the internet. Packages that are already installed and intact are left alone, unless force is set to download and install them again. Other tools install the packages they need on their own, so call this only to install ahead of time, such as before going offline, or when a tool returns a setup error with the install_packages action (for example when the engine was launched with automatic install turned off). A download can take a few minutes; the tool reports progress and can be cancelled.

inputSchema.description: Which packages to install or repair.

force.description:
Download and install the packages again even if they are installed,
replacing the installed copies. Use it when a package's tools fail in
ways that suggest damaged files. Defaults to false. Don't use it while
other operations are running.

packages.description:
Names of the packages to install or repair, as get_engine_info lists
them, such as oss-cad-suite. Omitted means every package in the
engine's manifest.

name: get_catalog
description: Returns board and FPGA definitions from the engine's read-only catalog. Use it to find a board's catalog ID, such as alhambra-ii, to pass as the board of other tools, or to see a board's FPGA and how it is programmed. Each section is returned only when asked for: {"boards": {"fetch": true}} returns all boards, and {"boards": {"fetch": true, "ids": ["alhambra-ii"]}} only the listed ones. Board descriptions are the boards' names for people.

fetch.description: Whether to return this section. Defaults to false.

ids.description:
Catalog IDs of the entries to return. Omitted means all entries. An
ID that isn't in the section is an error.

boards.description: Which boards to return. Omitted means none.

fpgas.description: Which FPGAs to return. Omitted means none.

name: lint
description: Checks Verilog and SystemVerilog sources for errors and likely mistakes with Verilator, without building, like apio lint. It is much faster than build and finds problems synthesis accepts, such as width mismatches. List the design files and, optionally, the testbenches; the engine doesn't search for them. The board selects the FPGA's primitive models, so designs that use them lint cleanly. Problems found are the result, not an error: passed is false and diagnostics lists each problem at file and line, with Verilator's warning code at the end of the text, which a /* verilator lint_off CODE */ comment can silence. The first call may install the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes. Writes nothing.

name: test
description: Runs testbenches with Icarus Verilog, like apio test: compiles the design files with each testbench, runs it, and reports whether it passed. A testbench fails by calling $fatal or $error, or by printing a failure line from Apio's assertion macros (*** ASSERTION FAILED or ERROR at file:line); it must end with $finish, and must not call $dumpfile, since the engine sets where its waveform goes (call $dumpvars to write one). Every listed testbench runs, even after one fails; each stops at its first failure unless stop_at_first_failure is false. A failing testbench is the result, not an error: passed is false, and each testbench's diagnostics and output say why. Compile errors are a design error with diagnostics at file and line. The first call may install the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes. To look at a testbench's signals in a waveform viewer, use simulate.

name: simulate
description: Simulates one testbench with Icarus Verilog and opens its waveform in GTKWave, like apio sim: compiles the design files with the testbench, runs it to write the waveform (.vcd) into the build folder, then starts GTKWave detached and returns without waiting for it. The testbench must call $dumpvars and $finish, and must not call $dumpfile. GTKWave opens the layout file (.gtkw), which holds the signals shown; when it is missing, or is still a default one, the engine writes a default with the testbench's top-level signals, deleted again when GTKWave exits unless the user saved it; a layout the user saved is kept. Set open_viewer to false to only write the waveform, such as when no one is at the screen. A failing testbench runs to the end and is shown, with passed false and GTKWave's marker at the first failure in a default layout. Compile errors are a design error with diagnostics at file and line. To just check whether testbenches pass, use test.

name: build
description: Builds an FPGA design into a bitstream: synthesizes the Verilog or SystemVerilog sources, places and routes them on the board's FPGA using the constraint file (.pcf, which maps top-level ports to pins), and packs the bitstream into the build folder. Give the source files explicitly; the engine doesn't search for them, though `include files are found next to the including file or in the source folder. A build with no changes since the last one returns at once with up_to_date set. The first build may install the toolchain package first, which takes a few minutes. Design problems come back as a design error with diagnostics at file and line. After a successful build, program_board programs the bitstream into the board.

The maximum frequency each clock can run at, in MHz, by clock net
name. A clock that misses its target isn't an error: compare these
with the design's needs.

up_to_date.description:
True if nothing had changed since the last build, so nothing was
rebuilt.

name: clean_build
description: Deletes build folders, like apio clean. Given a build folder, such as /home/u/proj/_build/default, it deletes it. Given a folder of build folders, such as /home/u/proj/_build, it deletes each build folder directly inside it, then the folder itself if nothing else is left. It only deletes folders the build tool made, so other files are never removed. A folder that doesn't exist is fine.

folder.description:
A build folder, or a folder whose direct subfolders are build
folders, as an absolute path. One of its last two folder names must
contain "build".

deleted.description:
The deleted folders, as absolute paths, including the given folder
when it was deleted. Empty when there was nothing to delete.

name: list_devices
description: Lists the USB devices connected to this computer, with their USB IDs, names and serial numbers. Given a board, each device also says whether it matches that board, which shows whether the board is connected and whether several are. Use it before program_board, or to find a board's serial number when several boards of the same kind are connected.

Architecture.description: FPGA families. Milestone 1 supports iCE40 only.

oneOf.description: Lattice iCE40.

BoardInputDefinition.description:
A board definition in a request. Like a catalog entry, except that the
FPGA can be given either as fpga_id or as a full fpga definition.

default_variant.description: The name of the programming variant used by default.

fpga.description: The board's FPGA as a full definition. Give either fpga_id or fpga.

fpga_id.description:
The board's FPGA as a catalog ID, such as ice40hx4k-tq144-8k. Give
either fpga_id or fpga.

variants.description: The ways to program the board, by variant name.

anyOf.description: A board's catalog ID, such as alhambra-ii. get_catalog lists them.
A full board definition, for boards that aren't in the catalog.

BoardSpec.description: A board: a catalog ID, or a full definition.

FpgaDefinition.description: An FPGA: its architecture, part and toolchain parameters.

nextpnr_device.description: The device type nextpnr uses, such as hx8k.

nextpnr_package.description: The package nextpnr uses, such as tq144:4k.

part_number.description: The vendor's part number, such as ICE40HX4K-TQ144.

ProgrammingVariant.description: One way to program a board, such as to flash with a particular cable.

args.description:
The programmer's arguments, as a template. The engine replaces
${VID}, ${PID}, ${BUS} and ${DEV} with the device's USB vendor ID,
product ID, bus and device number, ${SERIAL} with its serial number,
and ${BITSTREAM} with the bitstream path.

programmer.description: The programmer to run: openfpgaloader or iceprog.

usb.description: The USB filter that finds the board's device.

UsbFilter.description: Which USB devices are this board.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits, such as 6010.

product_regex.description:
A regular expression the device's product name must match, when
several boards share the same USB IDs. Omitted means any product name.

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits, such as 0403.

inputSchema.description: Optionally, a board to match the devices against.

board.description:
A board, as a catalog ID such as alhambra-ii or a full definition.
When given, each device reports whether it matches this board.

inputSchema.title: ListDevicesInput

device.description: USB device number on its bus.

manufacturer.description: The manufacturer name the device reports, when available.

matches_board.description:
Whether the device matches the given board. Present only when a board
was given.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits.

product.description: The product name the device reports, when available.

serial_number.description: The serial number the device reports, when available.

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits.

oneOf.description: A USB device.

devices.description:
The connected USB devices, sorted by vendor ID, product ID, bus and
device number.

name: program_board
description: Programs the bitstream of a successful build into the board it was built for. It doesn't build: call build first, and program_board only if the build succeeded. The board comes from the build, so it takes only the build folder. It finds the connected board by USB; if none is connected it returns a setup error with connect_board, and if several are, a setup error with select_device that lists them, so retry with one's serial_number. Most boards are programmed to flash, so the design stays after power-off.

inputSchema.description: Which build to program, and optionally which device.

build_folder.description: The build folder of a successful build, as an absolute path.

programmer_command.description:
A custom programmer command that replaces the board's default one,
like Apio's programmer_cmd. Its first word is a program from the
toolchain package, such as openFPGALoader, or an absolute path. It may
use ${VID}, ${PID}, ${BUS}, ${DEV}, ${SERIAL} and must use
${BITSTREAM}.

serial_number.description:
Program only the device with this serial number, when several
matching boards are connected.

verbose.description:
Let the programmer print more detail, shown in the live output and
the logs. Not applied to a programmer_command. Defaults to false.

inputSchema.title: ProgramBoardInput

device.description: USB device number on its bus.

manufacturer.description: The manufacturer name the device reports, when available.

matches_board.description:
Whether the device matches the given board. Present only when a board
was given.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits.

product.description: The product name the device reports, when available.

serial_number.description: The serial number the device reports, when available.

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits.

oneOf.description: A USB device.

programmer.description:
The programmer that was used, such as openfpgaloader, or custom for a
programmer_command.
